questions.stem: ___ the sales team exceeded its target, the bonuses were paid early.

fr.rule: Because + sujet + verbe exprime la cause.
why_wrong: A : demande un nom, pas une proposition.
C : demande un nom et exprime l'opposition.
D : adverbe de liaison, ne peut pas introduire une subordonnée.
fr.example: Because it rained, we stayed in.

why_wrong: A: needs a noun, not a clause.
C: needs a noun and expresses contrast.
D: a conjunctive adverb cannot introduce a subordinate clause.
en.example: Because it rained, we stayed in.

questions.stem: The product is expensive; ___, it is very durable.

fr.rule: Après un point-virgule, on emploie un adverbe de liaison (however) suivi d'une virgule.
why_wrong: A : exprime la cause, ce n'est pas le sens ici.
B : conjonction de subordination, pas après un point-virgule.
D : exprime la condition.
fr.example: It was late; however, we continued.

en.rule: After a semicolon use a conjunctive adverb (however) followed by a comma.
why_wrong: A: expresses cause, not the meaning here.
B: a subordinating conjunction, not used after a semicolon.
D: expresses condition.
en.example: It was late; however, we continued.

questions.stem: We will begin the meeting ___ everyone has arrived.

fr.rule: As soon as introduit une proposition de temps.
why_wrong: A : adverbe de liaison.
B : préposition, demande un nom.
D : exprime l'opposition, pas le temps.
fr.example: Call me as soon as you land.

en.rule: As soon as introduces a time clause.
why_wrong: A: conjunctive adverb.
B: preposition, needs a noun.
D: expresses contrast, not time.
en.example: Call me as soon as you land.

questions.stem: ___ you submit the form by Friday, your request cannot be processed.

fr.rule: Unless = if not : « sauf si vous envoyez le formulaire ».
why_wrong: A : adverbe de conséquence.
B : exprime l'opposition.
C : le sens serait inversé (condition positive).
fr.example: Unless you hurry, you will miss it.

en.rule: Unless = if not: 'if you do not submit the form'.
why_wrong: A: result adverb.
B: expresses contrast.
C: the meaning would be reversed (positive condition).
en.example: Unless you hurry, you will miss it.

questions.stem: Revenue increased this year, ___ expenses decreased.

fr.rule: Whereas oppose deux faits : le chiffre d'affaires monte, alors que les dépenses baissent.
why_wrong: A : exprime la condition.
B : exprime le but.
C : demande un nom.
fr.example: He likes tea, whereas she likes coffee.

en.rule: Whereas contrasts two facts: revenue rose while expenses fell.
why_wrong: A: expresses condition.
B: expresses purpose.
C: needs a noun.
en.example: He likes tea, whereas she likes coffee.

questions.stem: ___ the heavy traffic, the keynote speaker arrived on time.

why_wrong: A : Adverbe de liaison, il ne s'emploie pas devant un groupe nominal.
C : Sens de cause, faux ici : il y a une opposition.
D : « Although » introduit une proposition (sujet + verbe), pas un nom.
fr.example: Although it was late, we stayed.

why_wrong: A: A linking adverb; it does not precede a noun phrase.
C: Cause meaning, wrong here: the idea is contrast.
D: 'Although' introduces a clause (subject + verb), not a noun.
en.example: Although it was late, we stayed.

questions.stem: We will begin the presentation ___ everyone has taken a seat.

fr.rule: Once, as soon as, after + proposition = conjonction de temps.
why_wrong: A : Préposition : elle ne peut pas introduire une proposition.
C : « rather » seul n'est pas une conjonction de temps.
D : Préposition aussi, suivie d'un nom.

en.rule: Once, as soon as, after + clause = time conjunction.
why_wrong: A: A preposition: it cannot introduce a clause.
C: 'rather' alone is not a time conjunction.
D: Also a preposition, followed by a noun.

questions.stem: The new printer is ___ fast ___ reliable.

why_wrong: A : « either… or » exprime un choix, pas une addition.
B : « both » va avec « and ».
C : « neither » va avec « nor », pas « or ».
fr.example: He is both polite and efficient.

en.rule: Both… and: two items added together.
why_wrong: A: 'either… or' expresses a choice, not addition.
B: 'both' goes with 'and'.
C: 'neither' goes with 'nor', not 'or'.
en.example: He is both polite and efficient.
